arxiv-1805-03909.title: TADPOLE Challenge: Prediction of Longitudinal Evolution in Alzheimer’s Disease
arxiv-1805-03909.creator: Răzvan V. Marinescu, Neil P. Oxtoby, Alexandra L. Young, Esther E. Bron, Arthur W. Toga, Michael W. Weiner, Frederik Barkhof, Nick C. Fox, Stefan Klein, Daniel C. Alexander, the EuroPOND Consortium, for the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative
arxiv-1805-03909.description: Abstract The Alzheimer’s Disease Prediction Of Longitudinal Evolution (TADPOLE) Challenge compares the performance of algorithms at predicting future evolution of individuals at risk of Alzheimer’s disease. TADPOLE Challenge participants train their models and algorithms on historical data from the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) study or any other datasets to which they have access.

arxiv-2202-09028.title: On the Implicit Bias Towards Depth Minimization in Deep Neural Networks
arxiv-2202-09028.creator: Tomer Galanti, Liane Galanti, Ido Ben-Shaul
arxiv-2202-09028.description: Abstract Recent results in the literature suggest that the penultimate (second-to-last) layer representations of neural networks that are trained for classification exhibit a clustering property called neural collapse (NC). We study the implicit bias of stochastic gradient descent (SGD) in favor of low-depth solutions when training deep neural networks.

arxiv-2206-06641.title: Stellar limb darkening. Thanks: This work is not an official PLATO mission deliverable
arxiv-2206-06641.creator: N. M. Kostogryz ,, V. Witzke, A. I. Shapiro, S. K. Solanki, P. F. L. Maxted, R. L. Kurucz, L. Gizon
arxiv-2206-06641.description: Abstract Context. The detection of the first exoplanet paved the way into the era of transit photometry space missions with a revolutionary photometric precision that aim at discovering new exoplanetary systems around different types of stars. With this high precision, it is possible to derive very accurately the radii of exoplanets which is crucial for constraining their type and composition.

arxiv-2207-10733.title: GreenDB - A Dataset and Benchmark for Extraction of Sustainability Information of Consumer Goods
arxiv-2207-10733.creator: Sebastian Jäger, Alexander Flick, Jessica Adriana Sanchez Garcia, Kaspar von den Driesch, Karl Brendel, Felix Biessmann
arxiv-2207-10733.description: Abstract The production, shipping, usage, and disposal of consumer goods have a substantial impact on greenhouse gas emissions and the depletion of resources. Machine Learning (ML) can help to foster sustainable consumption patterns by accounting for sustainability aspects in product search or recommendations of modern retail platforms.

arxiv-2401-08787.title: Segment Anything Model Can Not Segment Anything: Assessing AI Foundation Model’s Generalizability in Permafrost Mapping
arxiv-2401-08787.creator: Wenwen Li 1, ∗ , Chia-Yu Hsu 1 , Sizhe Wang 1, 2 , Yezhou Yang 2 , Hyunho Lee 1 , Anna Liljedahl 3 , Chandi Witharana 4 , Yili Yang 3 , Brendan M. Rogers 3 , Samantha T. Arundel 5 , Matthew B. Jones 6 , Kenton McHenry 7 , and Patricia Solis 1
arxiv-2401-08787.description: Abstract This paper assesses trending AI foundation models, especially emerging computer vision foundation models and their performance in natural landscape feature segmentation. While the term foundation model has quickly garnered interest from the geospatial domain, its definition remains vague. Hence, this paper will first introduce AI foundation models and their defining characteristics.

arxiv-2409-16933.title: Construction of weak solutions to the equations of a compressible viscous model
arxiv-2409-16933.creator: Nilasis Chaudhuri, Piotr B. Mucha, Milan Pokorný
arxiv-2409-16933.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Nilasis Chaudhuri, Piotr B. Mucha, Milan Pokorný. The paper aims on the construction of weak solutions to equations of a model of compressible viscous fluids, being a simplification of the classical compressible Navier-Stokes system. We present a novel scheme for approximating systems that preserves structural integrity by avoiding classical regularization with − ϵ ​ 𝚫 ​ ϱ {\bf{-\epsilon\Delta\varrho}} , thus maintaining the transport character of the continuity equation.

arxiv-2503-04436.title: Relationship between the shear moduli and defect-induced structural relaxation of high-entropy metallic glasses
arxiv-2503-04436.creator: Andrey Makarov, Evgenia Gonchrova, Jichao Qiao, Roman Konchakov, Vitaly Khonik
arxiv-2503-04436.description: Abstract We performed high-frequency shear modulus and calorimetry measurements on seven high-entropy metallic glasses (HEMGs) in the initial, relaxed and crystalline states. It is shown that the shear modulus of HEMGs is intrinsically related with the concentration of defects responsible for structural relaxation.

arxiv-2508-14971.title: A Spectroscopic Hunt for Post-Red Supergiants in the Large Magellanic Cloud II: Turbulent Line Broadening in the Spectra of LMC Yellow Supergiants Journal: ApJ Facilities: Magellan:Clay (MIKE double echelle spectrograph), TESS ACID v0.1.0 ( Dolan et al. 2024 ) Astropy v6.1.0 ( Astropy Collaboration
arxiv-2508-14971.creator: Trevor Z. Dorn-Wallenstein, Kaitlyn M. Chen, Samantha C. Wu, Jared A. Goldberg, Anna J. G. O’Grady, Ayanna T. Mann, Poderosa I. Don-Wallanchez
arxiv-2508-14971.description: Abstract Massive stars in the Hertzsprung gap are a mixed population of objects in short-lived evolutionary phases: yellow supergiants (YSGs) evolving towards the red supergiant (RSG) phase, partially-stripped post-RSGs, and other, rarer outcomes of stellar evolution. Studies of sufficiently large samples of these objects can constrain massive star structure and evolution during these poorly-understood phases.

arxiv-2512-21729.title: Golden and Silver Dark Sirens for precise H 0 H_{0} measurement with HETDEX
arxiv-2512-21729.creator: Yixuan Dang, Ish Gupta, Robin Ciardullo, Erin Mentuch Cooper, Shiksha Pandey, Dustin Davis, Surhud More, Rachel Gray, Hsin-Yu Chen, Daniel J. Farrow, Caryl Gronwall, Donghui Jeong, Shun Saito, Donald P. Schneider, B. S. Sathyaprakash
arxiv-2512-21729.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yixuan Dang, Ish Gupta, Robin Ciardullo, Erin Mentuch Cooper, Shiksha Pandey, Dustin Davis, Surhud More, Rachel Gray, Hsin-Yu Chen, Daniel J. Farrow, Caryl Gronwall, Donghui Jeong, Shun Saito, Donald P. Schneider, B. S. Sathyaprakash. Gravitational waves (GWs) from compact binary coalescences are standard sirens that provide a direct measure of the source’s luminosity distance, enabling an independent measurement of the Hubble constant ( H 0 H_{0} ).

plos-pone-0004386.creator: Valentina Rosu, Niyaz Ahmed, Daniela Paccagnini et al.
plos-pone-0004386.description: PLOS ONE research article. Mycobacterium avium subspecies paratuberculosis (MAP) is a versatile pathogen with a broad host range. Its association with type-1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) has been recently proposed. Rapid identification of infectious agents such as MAP in diabetic patients at the level of clini

pmc-10604436.title: Impact of Met-Expectation of Athletic Justice on Athletic Satisfaction and Organizational Commitment via Leader–Member Exchange among Elite Saudi Arabian Athletes
pmc-10604436.creator: Seungmo Kim, Taeyeon Oh, Adam Love, Majed Essa Alahmad
pmc-10604436.description: Athletes’ perceptions of fairness toward coaching behaviors and decisions can play a crucial role in the development and maintenance of a strong coach–athlete relationship. However, scholars have given limited attention to athletes’ perceptions of fairness. Therefore, the current study aimed to explore the relationship between coaches and athletes by applying the concept of organizational justice based on met-expectation theory.

pmc-11392514.title: OnetoMap Meta-Data: Healthcare Analytics Through Research
pmc-11392514.creator: Nadayca Mateussi, Haroon Janjua, Emily A Grimsley, Melissa Kendall, Tyler Zander, Ricardo Pietrobon, Paul C Kuo
pmc-11392514.description: Introduction: Big Data has revolutionized healthcare research through the three Vs: volume, veracity, and variety. This study introduces the OnetoMap meta-data repository, a centralized inventory developed in collaboration with the University of South Florida's Department of Surgery.Methods: The repository offers extensive details about each database, including its primary purpose, available variables, and examples of high-impact research utilizing these databases.

pmc-11627368.title: Cell-free placental DNA: What do we really know?
pmc-11627368.creator: Natalie Yuen, Melanie Lemaire, Samantha L. Wilson
pmc-11627368.description: Cell-free placental DNA (cfpDNA) is present in maternal circulation during gestation. CfpDNA carries great potential as a research and clinical tool as it provides a means to investigate the placental (epi)genome across gestation, which previously required invasive placenta sampling procedures. CfpDNA has been widely implemented in the clinical setting for noninvasive prenatal testing (NIPT).

pmc-12443309.title: Optimization of skeleton structure discrimination standard for SMA-13 mixture based on high-temperature performance
pmc-12443309.creator: Jinshun Xue, Xiao Chen, Wei Zhao, Yuanyuan Wang
pmc-12443309.description: The stone–on–stone contact-interlocked skeleton structure of stone mastic asphalt (SMA) mixtures is crucial for the effective design of the mixture. However, existing skeleton structure discrimination standard (VCAmix < VCADRC) for SMA mixture gradation design is proven to necessitate calibration. To address this, a method was developed to analyse the influence of structural parameters on the high-temperature performance of SMA-13 mixture.

pmc-12476796.title: Pre-hospital proton pump inhibitor use and clinical outcomes in hospitalized COVID-19 patients: A retrospective case-control study
pmc-12476796.creator: Harinivaas Shanmugavel Geetha, Sushmita Prabhu, Mithil Gowda Suresh, George M Abraham, Akshaya Sekar, Safia Mohamed, Abinesh Sekar, Juniali Hatwal, Aalam Sohal, Akash Batta
pmc-12476796.description: BACKGROUNDProton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are among the most commonly prescribed medications globally. While concerns exist regarding their association with adverse infection-related outcomes, their impact on coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) severity remains uncertain. Emerging preclinical data suggest immunomodulatory and antiviral properties of PPIs, yet clinical evidence is conflicting.

pmc-12608272.title: Education, Sex, and Age Shape Rey Complex Figure Performance in Cognitively Normal Adults: An Interpretable Machine Learning Study
pmc-12608272.creator: Albert J. B. Lee, Benjamin Zhao, James J. Lah, Samantha E. John, David W. Loring, Cassie S. Mitchell
pmc-12608272.description: Background: Demographic factors such as education, sex, and age can significantly influence cognitive test performance, yet their impact on the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) and Rey Complex Figure (CF) test has not been fully characterized in large, cognitively normal samples. Understanding these effects is critical for refining normative standards and improving the clinical interpretation of neuropsychological assessments.

pmc-13328315.title: Burden of invasive group a streptococcus infection in Australia: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13328315.creator: Himali Ratnayake, Damon Eisen, Oyelola Adegboye, Anton Pak, Chanika Alahakoon, Mohabeer Teeluck, Gbeminiyi Richard Otolorin, Emma McBryde
pmc-13328315.description: PurposeIn this study, we aimed to estimate the burden of invasive Group A Streptococcus (iGAS) infection in Australia and describe the risk factors and outcomes across regions and populations.MethodsStudies published in six databases until October 2025 were included. The first study included in the systematic review was published in 1996. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42023493112).

pmc-13393726.title: Deep care: a qualitative analysis of black community midwifery
pmc-13393726.creator: Kaytura Felix, Chinmayee Balachandra, Alejandro McGhee, Jay Mawuli, Keshia Pollack Porter, Dána-Ain Davis
pmc-13393726.description: BackgroundBlack community midwifery has historically offered holistic, culturally grounded care for Black birthing people, yet remains marginalized within modern maternity systems. As disparities in Black maternal health outcomes persist, this qualitative study explored the values, services, and impacts of Black community midwifery across multiple U.S. regions.

pmc-13455404.title: Retroesophageal aberrant right subclavian artery associated with a non-recurrent laryngeal nerve and absent right internal thoracic artery: a donor case report
pmc-13455404.creator: Athinan Prommahom, Natch Supawatanakul, Napat Manasboonpermpool, Roojanaat Meesomboon, Donttarat Jutamaneeroj, Pathorn Boongird, Penpicha Teerapatpondchai
pmc-13455404.description: BackgroundThe aberrant right subclavian artery (ARSA) is the most common anomaly of the arch of aorta and is significantly associated with a non-recurrent laryngeal nerve (NRLN). Nevertheless, the co-occurrence of ARSA with complex thoracic wall vascular remodeling is scarcely described in the current literature. This exploration describes an unusual group of neurovascular variations with important surgical significance.

pmc-13545648.title: Triacylglycerol synthesis in microalgae under abiotic stress: an updated integrative review
pmc-13545648.creator: Vipul Swarup Bhatnagar, Marta Saldat, Agnieszka Zienkiewicz, Zhi-Yan Du, Krzysztof Zienkiewicz
pmc-13545648.description: Microalgae exhibit remarkable metabolic plasticity, rapidly redirecting carbon toward triacylglycerol (TAG) accumulation under environmental stress. In this review, we synthesize recent advances in understanding how nutrient limitation, light fluctuations, salinity, temperature extremes, and chemical modulators regulate TAG biosynthesis in diverse microalgal systems.

pmc-13662783.title: Dustiness of graphene and graphite
pmc-13662783.creator: Douglas E Evans, M Christina Kander, Chen Wang, Peter B Shaw, Seth McCormick, Kabir Rishi, Terrence S Kuca, Derek E Stinson, Gregory J Deye, Matthew M Dahm
pmc-13662783.description: Graphene is among the most utilized nanoscale materials in the United States. It is a single-layer carbonaceous nanoscale material with a hexagonal structure. Subtractive synthesis from graphite is common in high-volume manufacturing, with graphene and graphite often present within the same workplace. There is little worker exposure data available to inform risk assessments, particularly for graphene.

the-woman-with-the-fan.creator: Hichens, Robert
